weeks.title: Gadgets as systems: batteries, chargers and resistance
weeks.summary: Is week aap phone jaise gadget ko blocks ke system ki tarah dekhna seekhoge, battery capacity (mAh, Wh) aur charger power ka hisaab lagaoge, back-of-the-envelope estimates karoge, aur resistance R = ρL/A samjhoge.
concepts: **System view**: ek smartphone ko blocks me todo: battery + power management, processor aur memory, display, sensors (camera, mic, accelerometer), radio (WiFi, 4G/5G, Bluetooth) aur audio (speaker). Har block ka kaam hai input lena, process karna aur output dena. Engineer pehle blocks aur unke beech energy/signal ka flow dekhta hai, details baad me.

**Battery capacity**: mAh charge ki unit hai (1 mAh = 1 mA ko 1 ghante tak dena = 3.6 C). Energy nikalni ho to voltage se multiply karo: **Energy (Wh) = V × Ah**. Jaise 5000 mAh, 3.85 V battery = 5 Ah × 3.85 V = 19.25 Wh. 1 Wh = 3600 J.

**Charger power**: P = V × I. Normal USB charger 5 V × 2 A = 10 W, fast charger 9 V × 2 A = 18 W ya isse zyada. Charging time ka rough estimate = battery energy ÷ (charger power × efficiency). Asli me end ke 20% me charging slow ho jaati hai, isliye time thoda zyada lagta hai.

**Back-of-the-envelope estimate**: exact data ke bina round numbers se answer ka order of magnitude nikaalna. Units hamesha saath likho, aur end me sanity check karo: kya answer realistic lagta hai? Jaise phone ko roz full charge karne ka saal bhar ka bill ₹100 se kam hi hoga.

**Resistance aur resistivity**: R = ρL/A. ρ (resistivity) material ki property hai (copper ≈ 1.7 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m), L length aur A cross-section area. Lamba wire = zyada R, mota wire = kam R. Isliye heavy current wale cables mote hote hain.
**Unit prefixes**: m = 10⁻³, μ = 10⁻⁶, n = 10⁻⁹, k = 10³, M = 10⁶. 1 mm² = 10⁻⁶ m² (kyunki 1 mm = 10⁻³ m, aur area me square hota hai). Unit conversion ki galti circuits me sabse common galti hai.

**Efficiency**: koi bhi conversion (wall AC se battery DC, ya 3.7 V se 5 V power bank output) 100% efficient nahi hota. Output energy = efficiency × input energy, baaki heat ban jaati hai. Isliye charger aur power bank garam hote hain.

example.problem: Ek phone ki battery 4000 mAh, 3.8 V hai. Use 20 W charger se 0% se 100% charge karna hai, aur charging path ki efficiency 80% hai. Lagbhag kitna time lagega?
steps: Battery energy = 4 Ah × 3.8 V = 15.2 Wh.
Battery tak pahunchne wali power = 20 W × 0.8 = 16 W.
Time = energy ÷ power = 15.2 Wh ÷ 16 W = 0.95 h.
Sanity check: fast charging phones sach me lagbhag 1 ghante me charge hote hain, to answer realistic hai.
Answer: **lagbhag 57 minute** (asli me thoda zyada, kyunki end me charging slow hoti hai).

mistakes: mAh ko seedha energy samajh lena. Do batteries ke voltages alag hon to sirf mAh compare karna galat hai; Wh = V × Ah compare karo.
mm² ko m² me badalte waqt 10⁻³ se multiply kar dena. Area me square lagta hai: 1 mm² = 10⁻⁶ m².
Efficiency bhool jaana. Wall se li gayi energy hamesha battery me store hui energy se zyada hoti hai.
revision: P = V × I; charging time ≈ energy ÷ (power × efficiency).
R = ρL/A: length double ⇒ R double, area double ⇒ R half.
Estimate karte waqt units saath rakho aur end me sanity check karo.

questions.question: Ek phone battery par likha hai 5000 mAh, 3.7 V. Isme kitni energy store hai?
questions.explanation: Energy = V × Ah = 3.7 V × 5 Ah = 18.5 Wh. 18500 Wh tab aata hai jab mAh ko Ah me badalna (÷1000) bhool jaate ho, aur 1.35 Wh tab jab multiply ki jagah divide kar dete ho.

questions.question: Ek fast charger 9 V par 2 A current deta hai. Charger ki output power kitni hai?
questions.explanation: P = V × I = 9 V × 2 A = 18 W. 4.5 W to V/I hai (jo resistance jaisi quantity hai, power nahi), aur 11 W tab aata hai jab V aur I ko add kar dete ho.

questions.question: Copper wire ki length 10 m aur cross-section area 1 mm² hai. Copper ki resistivity ρ = 1.7 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m lo. Wire ka resistance kitna hai?
questions.explanation: A = 1 mm² = 10⁻⁶ m². R = ρL/A = 1.7 × 10⁻⁸ × 10 / 10⁻⁶ = 0.17 Ω. Agar mm² ko galti se 10⁻³ m² le liya to 1.7 × 10⁻⁴ Ω aata hai — area me square lagana mat bhoolo.

questions.question: Resistance R wale ek wire ko kheench kar uski length double kar di, volume same rehta hai. Naya resistance kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: Volume = L × A same hai, to L double hone par A half ho jaata hai. R = ρL/A me L ×2 aur A ÷2, isliye R ×4 = 4R. 2R wala trap tab aata hai jab sirf length ka effect dekhte ho aur patla hona bhool jaate ho.

questions.question: Power bank: 10000 mAh, 3.7 V cells, aur phone tak energy pahunchane ki efficiency 80%. Phone battery: 3000 mAh, 3.85 V. Power bank lagbhag kitni baar phone ko 0% se full charge kar sakta hai?
questions.explanation: Power bank energy = 10 Ah × 3.7 V = 37 Wh; phone tak pahunchti hai 37 × 0.8 = 29.6 Wh. Phone battery = 3 Ah × 3.85 V = 11.55 Wh. 29.6 / 11.55 ≈ 2.6. 3.3 tab aata hai jab sirf mAh ka ratio (10000/3000) le lete ho — voltage aur efficiency dono chhoot jaate hain.

questions.question: Ek phone ki 15 Wh battery saal ke 365 din roz ek baar full charge hoti hai. Charger efficiency 75% hai aur bijli ₹8 per kWh hai. Saal bhar ka charging ka kharcha lagbhag kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Roz wall se energy = 15 / 0.75 = 20 Wh. Saal me 20 × 365 = 7300 Wh = 7.3 kWh. Kharcha = 7.3 × 8 ≈ ₹58. Efficiency bhoolne par 5.475 kWh × 8 ≈ ₹44 aata hai, aur Wh ko kWh me na badalne par ₹5840 jaisa absurd number.

weeks.title: Circuit laws: Ohm, Kirchhoff, nodes and meshes
weeks.summary: Is week aap voltage, current aur Ohm's law se shuru karke ideal sources, I-V graphs, KCL/KVL, series-parallel, nodal aur mesh analysis seekhoge, aur capacitor/inductor ka basic behaviour samjhoge.
concepts: **Voltage, current, power**: voltage do points ke beech energy per charge ka difference hai (V = J/C), current charge ka flow rate hai (A = C/s). Element ki power P = V × I. **Ohm's law**: resistor ke liye V = I × R, yaani V aur I proportional hain.

**Ideal sources**: ideal voltage source apne terminals par fixed voltage rakhta hai, current chahe jitna ho (circuit decide karta hai). Ideal current source fixed current deta hai, voltage circuit decide karta hai. Asli battery = ideal voltage source + chhota internal resistance.

**I-V characteristic**: V ko x-axis aur I ko y-axis par lo. Resistor: origin se seedhi line, slope 1/R. Ideal voltage source: V = Vs par vertical line. Ideal current source: I = Is par horizontal line. Graph dekh kar element pehchaana ja sakta hai.

**KCL aur KVL**: KCL — kisi node me aane wala total current = jaane wala total current (charge jama nahi hota). KVL — kisi bhi closed loop me voltages ka algebraic sum = 0 (energy conservation). Saari circuit analysis inhi do laws par tiki hai.

**Series aur parallel**: series me R_eq = R1 + R2 + ... (same current). Parallel me 1/R_eq = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ... (same voltage); do resistors ke liye R1R2/(R1 + R2). **Voltage divider**: V_out = V_in × R2/(R1 + R2), par sirf jab output par load na ho.

**Nodal analysis**: ek node ko ground (0 V) chuno, baaki nodes ke voltages unknown rakho, har unknown node par KCL likho (sab currents ko node voltages me likho), aur equations solve karo. **Mesh analysis**: har mesh me ek loop current maan kar KVL likho. Jitne kam unknowns, utna aasaan.
**Capacitor**: Q = CV, current i = C dv/dt. DC steady state me current zero, yaani capacitor open circuit jaisa. Iska voltage achaanak jump nahi kar sakta. Stored energy = ½CV².
**Inductor**: v = L di/dt. DC steady state me voltage zero, yaani short circuit jaisa. Iska current achaanak jump nahi kar sakta. Stored energy = ½LI².

example.problem: Neeche ke circuit me nodal analysis se V_A aur V_B nikaalo. 12 V source ka − terminal ground par hai.
steps: Unknowns: V_A aur V_B (ground = 0 V).
Node A par KCL (sab currents bahar jaate maano): (V_A − 12)/3 + V_A/6 + (V_A − V_B)/2 = 0.
Node B par KCL: (V_B − V_A)/2 + V_B/4 = 0 ⇒ 3V_B = 2V_A ⇒ V_B = 2V_A/3.
Pehli equation ko 6 se multiply karo: 2V_A − 24 + V_A + 3V_A − 3V_B = 0 ⇒ 6V_A − 3V_B = 24.
V_B = 2V_A/3 rakho: 6V_A − 2V_A = 24 ⇒ V_A = 6 V, aur V_B = 4 V.
Check (series-parallel se): 2 + 4 = 6 Ω, jo 6 Ω ke parallel me 3 Ω; divider se V_A = 12 × 3/(3 + 3) = 6 V ✓.
Answer: **V_A = 6 V, V_B = 4 V**.

mistakes: Loaded divider me bhi seedha R2/(R1 + R2) laga dena. Output par load ho to pehle R2 aur load ka parallel nikaalo, phir divider lagao.
KCL likhte waqt current directions mix karna. Ek rule rakho: har current ko node se bahar jaata maano; answer negative aaye to direction ulti hai.
Capacitor ko DC par short samajhna (aur inductor ko open). Ulta hai: DC steady state me capacitor open, inductor short.
revision: KCL: node par currents ka sum 0; KVL: loop me voltages ka sum 0.
Series: R add karo; parallel: 1/R add karo.
Capacitor: i = C dv/dt, E = ½CV²; inductor: v = L di/dt, E = ½LI².
I-V graph: resistor sloped line, voltage source vertical, current source horizontal.

questions.question: 2 Ω, 3 Ω aur 6 Ω teeno parallel me hain. Equivalent resistance kitna hai?
questions.explanation: 1/R = 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = 3/6 + 2/6 + 1/6 = 1, to R = 1 Ω. 11 Ω series ka answer hai. Yaad rakho, parallel ka R sabse chhote resistor (2 Ω) se bhi kam hota hai.

questions.question: I-V graph me V x-axis par aur I y-axis par hai. Ek ideal 2 A current source ka graph kaisa dikhega?
options: Origin se jaati seedhi line jiska slope 2 hai
Origin se jaati seedhi line jiska slope 1/2 hai
questions.explanation: Ideal current source har voltage par same current deta hai, isliye graph I = 2 A par horizontal line hai. Vertical line ideal voltage source ki hoti hai, aur origin se jaati line resistor ki.

questions.question: 12 V source ke saath 4 kΩ (upar) aur 4 kΩ (neeche) ka voltage divider bana hai. Neeche wale 4 kΩ ke across ek 4 kΩ load laga diya. Load par voltage kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Neeche 4 kΩ ∥ 4 kΩ = 2 kΩ. Divider: 12 × 2/(4 + 2) = 4 V. 6 V tab aata hai jab load ko ignore karke unloaded divider ka formula laga dete ho.

questions.question: 100 μF capacitor ko 10 V tak charge kiya. Usme store charge aur energy kitni hai?
questions.explanation: Q = CV = 100 × 10⁻⁶ × 10 = 10⁻³ C = 1 mC. E = ½CV² = ½ × 100 × 10⁻⁶ × 100 = 5 mJ. 10 mJ wala trap ½ bhoolne se aata hai (CV² le liya).

questions.question: 2 mH inductor ka current 1 ms me uniformly 0 se 3 A tak badhta hai. Is dauraan inductor ke across voltage kitna hai?
questions.explanation: v = L di/dt = 2 × 10⁻³ × (3 / 10⁻³) = 6 V. 6 mV tab aata hai jab sirf L × Δi le lete ho aur Δt (1 ms) se divide karna bhool jaate ho.

questions.question: Neeche ke circuit me 4 Ω resistor se kitna current ground ki taraf jaata hai? Dono sources ka − terminal ground par hai.
questions.explanation: Beech wale node ka voltage V maano. KCL: (V − 10)/2 + V/4 + (V − 6)/2 = 0. 4 se multiply: 2V − 20 + V + 2V − 12 = 0 ⇒ 5V = 32 ⇒ V = 6.4 V. 4 Ω me current = 6.4/4 = 1.6 A. 1.8 A to left wale 2 Ω ka current hai, aur 2.0 A tab aata hai jab 4 Ω ko ignore karke (10 − 6)/2 le lete ho.

weeks.title: Sound, sinusoids and the electricity bill
weeks.summary: Is week aap mic, speaker aur motor/generator ka working idea, sinusoid ke amplitude-frequency-phase, RMS value, harmonics, aur ghar ki 230 V, 50 Hz supply se kWh bill ka hisaab seekhoge.
concepts: **Transducer**: jo ek form ki energy ko doosri me badle. Dynamic **microphone** me sound pressure ek diaphragm aur coil ko magnet ke paas hilata hai, aur Faraday ke law se coil me voltage induce hota hai. **Speaker** ulta kaam karta hai: coil me current + magnetic field = force, jo cone ko hila kar sound banata hai.

**Motor aur generator**: ek hi machine ke do roop. Current do to shaft ghoomta hai (motor); shaft ghumao to voltage banta hai (generator). Cycle ki dynamo light aur power station ka generator isi principle par chalte hain.

**Sinusoid**: v(t) = A sin(2πft + φ). A = amplitude (peak), f = frequency (Hz), T = 1/f period, ω = 2πf angular frequency (rad/s), φ = phase (shift). Jaise v(t) = 5 sin(100πt) me ω = 100π, to f = 50 Hz.

**RMS value**: V_rms = √(mean of v²). Ye wo DC value hai jo resistor me utni hi average power degi. Sinusoid ke liye V_rms = V_peak/√2 ≈ 0.707 V_peak. Average power in R = V_rms²/R. Square wave (±A) ka rms = A.

**Harmonics**: koi bhi periodic signal = fundamental frequency f + uske integer multiples (2f, 3f, ...) ke sinusoids ka sum. Alag-alag frequencies ke sinusoids ki average powers seedhe add hoti hain: V_rms² = V1_rms² + V2_rms² + .... Isi wajah se guitar aur flute ka same note alag sunai deta hai.
**Household supply**: India me 230 V rms, 50 Hz. Peak = 230 × √2 ≈ 325 V. Appliances par likhi rating (V, W) rms values me hoti hai.

**Energy bill**: 1 unit = 1 kWh = 1000 W ka appliance 1 ghante chale. Energy (kWh) = power (kW) × time (h). Monthly bill = total units × rate per unit. Badi power wale aur zyada der chalne wale appliances (AC, geyser) bill ka bada hissa hote hain.

example.problem: 1.5 kW ka geyser roz 40 minute chalta hai. 30 din me kitne units lagenge, aur ₹7 per unit par kharcha kitna hoga?
steps: Roz ka time = 40/60 h = 2/3 h.
Roz ki energy = 1.5 kW × 2/3 h = 1 kWh.
30 din ki energy = 30 kWh = 30 units.
Answer: **30 units, ₹210**.

mistakes: 230 V ko peak samajh lena. 230 V rms hai; peak lagbhag 325 V hota hai.
Do frequencies wale signal ka rms nikaalte waqt amplitudes ko pehle add kar dena. Alag frequencies ke liye powers (squares) add hoti hain, amplitudes nahi.
W aur kWh mix karna. Power W/kW me hoti hai, energy kWh me; minutes ko hours me badalna mat bhoolo.
revision: Sinusoid: V_rms = V_peak/√2; 230 V rms ⇒ 325 V peak.
Alag frequencies: V_rms² = sum of individual V_rms².

questions.question: Ghar ki supply 230 V rms hai. Uska peak voltage lagbhag kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Sinusoid me V_peak = √2 × V_rms = 1.414 × 230 ≈ 325 V. 163 V tab aata hai jab √2 se multiply ki jagah divide kar dete ho, aur 460 V peak-to-peak jaisa galat double hai (asli peak-to-peak ≈ 650 V hota hai).

questions.question: v(t) = 5 sin(100πt + π/4) volt. Is signal ki frequency kya hai?
questions.explanation: Form A sin(ωt + φ) me ω = 100π rad/s. f = ω/2π = 100π/2π = 50 Hz. 314 Hz to ω ki value (100π ≈ 314) hai jo rad/s me hai, Hz me nahi. π/4 sirf phase hai, frequency par asar nahi.

questions.question: 60 W, 230 V rms ka bulb (ise ek resistor maano) 230 V rms supply par jal raha hai. Bulb ke current ka peak value lagbhag kitna hai?
questions.explanation: I_rms = P/V_rms = 60/230 ≈ 0.261 A. Peak = √2 × 0.261 ≈ 0.37 A. 0.26 A rms value hai (peak nahi), 0.18 A me √2 se galti se divide kiya gaya hai, aur 3.83 A = 230/60 hai jo galat formula hai.

questions.question: Ek ghar me 1.5 kW ka AC roz 8 ghante aur 75 W ka fan roz 10 ghante chalta hai. 30 din ka bill ₹6 per unit par kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: AC: 1.5 × 8 × 30 = 360 kWh. Fan: 0.075 × 10 × 30 = 22.5 kWh. Total 382.5 kWh × ₹6 = ₹2295. ₹2160 me fan chhoot gaya, ₹3510 me 75 W ko galti se 0.75 kW le liya, aur ₹76.5 sirf ek din ka kharcha hai.

questions.question: Ek square wave 0 V aur 10 V ke beech switch karti hai, dono levels par barabar time (50% duty). Iska RMS value kitna hai?
questions.explanation: v² aadha time 100 aur aadha time 0 hai, to mean of v² = 50. RMS = √50 ≈ 7.07 V. 5 V average (mean) value hai, rms nahi; sinusoid wala ÷√2 rule yahan apply nahi hota.

questions.question: Ek audio signal v(t) = 3 sin(ωt) + 4 sin(3ωt) volt hai (fundamental + 3rd harmonic). Ise 10 Ω speaker (resistor maano) par lagaya. Average power kitni hai?
questions.explanation: Alag frequencies ki powers add hoti hain: V_rms² = 3²/2 + 4²/2 = 4.5 + 8 = 12.5. P = 12.5/10 = 1.25 W. 2.45 W tab aata hai jab amplitudes add karke (3 + 4 = 7) 7²/2 le lete ho, aur 2.5 W tab jab 3² + 4² = 25 me /2 bhool jaate ho.

weeks.title: Resistive network tricks: bounds, ladders, bridges, symmetry
weeks.summary: Is week aap bade resistor networks ko smart tareeke se solve karna seekhoge: pehle bounds se answer ka range, phir ladder ko end se solve karna, balanced Wheatstone bridge, aur symmetry se resistive cube jaise problems.
concepts: **Bounds pehle**: series combination hamesha sabse bade resistor se bada hota hai, aur parallel combination sabse chhote se chhota. Kisi bhi resistor ko badhane se network ka R_eq kabhi kam nahi hota (aur ghatane se kabhi badhta nahi). Calculation se pehle range nikaal lo, galat answer turant pakda jaayega.

**Ladder network**: series aur shunt resistors ki seedhi. Hamesha far end se shuru karo: last shunt aur termination ko combine karo, phir series jodo, phir agla shunt parallel me — aise input tak aao. R-2R ladder (series R, shunt 2R, end me 2R) har node par R dikhata hai, aur input par 2R.

**Infinite ladder**: ek section hata do to bacha hua ladder bhi wahi R_eq dikhata hai (self-similar). Series R1 aur shunt R2 ke liye: R_eq = R1 + (R2 ∥ R_eq), jo quadratic R_eq² − R1·R_eq − R1·R2 = 0 deta hai; positive root lo.

**Wheatstone bridge**: chaar arms P, Q, R, S aur beech me galvanometer. Agar P/Q = R/S (balanced), to bridge ke dono ends ka voltage barabar hai aur beech me current zero. Tab beech wale element ko hata sakte ho (ya short kar sakte ho) — answer same aayega.
**Symmetry**: agar circuit me do nodes symmetry ki wajah se same voltage par hain, to unhe jod sakte ho ya unke beech ka resistor hata sakte ho. Symmetric branches me current barabar baantta hai.
**Resistive cube** (12 edges, har ek R): body diagonal ke across 5R/6, face diagonal ke across 3R/4, ek edge ke across 7R/12. Ye symmetry se nikalte hain, ratne ki zaroorat nahi.

example.problem: 12 equal resistors R se bane cube me ek corner A se opposite corner B (body diagonal) ke beech equivalent resistance nikaalo.
steps: A me current I daalo aur B se nikaalo.
A se 3 edges nikalti hain, teeno symmetric hain, to har ek me I/3.
Un 3 corners se 6 edges aage jaati hain (har corner se 2), symmetry se har ek me I/6.
Phir 3 edges B me milti hain, har ek me I/3.
Kisi bhi path A → B par voltage drop: V = R·I/3 + R·I/6 + R·I/3 = 5IR/6.
R_eq = V/I = 5R/6. R = 12 Ω ho to R_eq = 10 Ω.
Answer: **R_AB = 5R/6**.

mistakes: Unbalanced bridge me bhi beech ka resistor hata dena. Ye trick sirf tab chalti hai jab P/Q = R/S ho.
Infinite ladder ko 1-2 sections par truncate karke answer maan lena. Self-similarity wali equation likho aur solve karo.
Ladder ko input side se solve karne ki koshish karna. Hamesha far end se shuru karo.
revision: Series ≥ sabse bada, parallel ≤ sabse chhota.
Balanced bridge: P/Q = R/S ⇒ beech me current 0.
Cube: body diagonal 5R/6, face diagonal 3R/4, edge 7R/12.
Same-potential nodes ko jod sakte ho.

questions.question: Wheatstone bridge me P = 10 Ω, Q = 20 Ω, R = 15 Ω hain. Balance ke liye (P/Q = R/S) S kitna hona chahiye?
questions.explanation: P/Q = R/S ⇒ S = R·Q/P = 15 × 20/10 = 30 Ω. 7.5 Ω tab aata hai jab ratio ulta laga dete ho (S = P·R/Q).

questions.question: 10 Ω, 20 Ω aur 30 Ω parallel me hain. Bina pura calculation kiye, equivalent ke baare me kya pakka sach hai?
questions.explanation: Parallel combination hamesha sabse chhote resistor (10 Ω) se kam hota hai, kyunki har naya path current ka extra raasta deta hai. Exact value 60/11 ≈ 5.45 Ω hai. Average lena series/parallel ka mix-up hai.

questions.question: Neeche R-2R ladder hai, R = 1 kΩ. Terminals A aur B ke beech resistance kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Far end se: 2R ∥ 2R = R. Usme series R jodo = 2R, phir agle 2R ke parallel = R. Phir se + R = 2R, ∥ 2R = R. Aakhir me pehla series R: R + R = 2R = 2 kΩ. 1 kΩ tab aata hai jab A ke paas wala pehla series R bhool jaate ho.

questions.question: Ek cube ki har edge 12 Ω ka resistor hai. Body diagonal ke opposite corners ke beech resistance kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Symmetry se current 3 → 6 → 3 edges me I/3, I/6, I/3 baantta hai. V = R(1/3 + 1/6 + 1/3)I = 5RI/6, to R_eq = 5 × 12/6 = 10 Ω. 9 Ω face diagonal (3R/4) ka answer hai aur 7 Ω ek edge (7R/12) ka.

questions.question: Ek 6 Ω resistor ke series me ek block hai. Block = 3 Ω ke parallel me koi unknown resistive network (resistance positive par pata nahi). Poore combination ke baare me kya pakka keh sakte ho?
questions.explanation: 3 Ω ke parallel me kuch bhi lagao, result 0 aur 3 Ω ke beech hi rahega. Series me 6 Ω jodne par total 6 Ω aur 9 Ω ke beech. 7.5 Ω tab aata hai jab unknown ko bhi 3 Ω maan lete ho — bina wajah assumption.

questions.question: Ek infinite ladder me har section me 2 Ω series aur 12 Ω shunt hai. Input par equivalent resistance kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Self-similarity: R = 2 + (12 ∥ R) = 2 + 12R/(12 + R). Solve: R² − 2R − 24 = 0 ⇒ (R − 6)(R + 4) = 0 ⇒ R = 6 Ω. 14 Ω sirf ek section (2 + 12) ka answer hai aur 8.46 Ω do sections ka — truncate karna galat hai.

weeks.title: Mixing signals: linearity and superposition
weeks.summary: Is week aap resistors se analog audio mixer banana seekhoge, linearity (additivity + homogeneity) samjhoge, aur superposition se multiple sources wale circuits ek-ek source le kar solve karoge.
concepts: **Linearity**: system linear hai agar do baatein sach hon. Additivity: input x1 ka output y1 aur x2 ka y2 ho, to x1 + x2 ka output y1 + y2. Homogeneity: input k guna karo to output bhi k guna. Resistors aur independent sources wale circuits linear hote hain.

**Superposition**: kai independent sources wale linear circuit me koi bhi voltage/current = har source ke akele contribution ka sum. Ek source rakho, baaki band karo: **voltage source band = short circuit** (0 V), **current source band = open circuit** (0 A). Phir saare contributions sign ke saath jodo.

**Resistive mixer**: kai signals V1, V2, ... ko resistors R1, R2, ... se ek common node par jodo. Agar output par load RL hai, to V_out = (V1/R1 + V2/R2 + ...)/(1/R1 + 1/R2 + ... + 1/RL). Ise Millman ka formula bhi kehte hain; ye KCL se seedha nikalta hai.

**Equal resistors, no load**: sab R barabar aur output open ho to V_out = inputs ka simple average. Chhote resistor wala input zyada weight paata hai, isliye resistor values se har channel ka volume (weight) set hota hai.

**Passive mixer ki limitation**: output hamesha inputs ke weighted average se chhota ya barabar hota hai (gain ≤ 1), aur load lagne par aur gir jaata hai. Isliye asli mixers me op-amp lagta hai (week 6).
**Power superpose nahi hoti**: P = V²/R quadratic hai, linear nahi. Pehle superposition se total voltage/current nikaalo, phir power nikaalo. Individual powers jodna galat hai.

example.problem: Do inputs V1 = 2 V aur V2 = −1 V, dono 10 kΩ ke through ek node se jude hain, aur node se ground tak 10 kΩ load hai. Superposition se V_out nikaalo.
steps: Sirf V1: V2 ko short (0 V) karo. Ab V2 wala 10 kΩ aur load 10 kΩ parallel = 5 kΩ.
Sirf V2: V1 ko short karo. Divider same hai: V_out2 = −1 × 5/15 = −0.333 V.
Answer: **V_out ≈ 0.33 V**.

mistakes: Voltage source ko band karte waqt open kar dena. Voltage source band = short; current source band = open.
Contributions jodte waqt sign bhool jaana. Negative source ka contribution negative hi hoga.
Har source ki power alag nikaal kar jod dena. Power quadratic hai; pehle total voltage nikaalo, phir V²/R.
revision: Superposition: voltage source → short, current source → open.

questions.question: Superposition lagate waqt, jis independent voltage source ka contribution abhi nahi dekh rahe, use kis se replace karte hain?
options: Use waise hi rehne dete hain
Utni hi value ke current source se
questions.explanation: Source ko band karne ka matlab hai uski value zero karna. 0 V ka voltage source ek wire jaisa hai, isliye short circuit. Open circuit current source ke liye hota hai (0 A) — dono ko ulta karna sabse common galti hai.

questions.question: Do mic signals 0.6 V aur 0.2 V, barabar resistors ke through ek common node par jode gaye. Output node par koi load nahi hai. Output voltage kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Equal resistors aur no load: KCL se (0.6 − V)/R + (0.2 − V)/R = 0 ⇒ V = 0.4 V, yaani simple average. 0.8 V seedha sum hai — passive resistor mixer signals ko add nahi, average karta hai.

questions.question: Mixer me V1 = 1 V, 10 kΩ ke through aur V2 = 4 V, 20 kΩ ke through ek node se jude hain. Output open hai (no load). V_out kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Millman: V_out = (1/10 + 4/20)/(1/10 + 1/20) = 0.3/0.15 = 2 V. Weight 1/R hota hai, isliye 10 kΩ wala V1 zyada pull karta hai. 3 V tab aata hai jab weights R se (1×10 + 4×20)/30 le lete ho — ulta weighting. 2.5 V simple average hai.

questions.question: Ek linear resistive circuit ke do inputs (V1, V2) hain. (V1, V2) = (2 V, 0 V) par output 1 V hai, aur (0 V, 3 V) par output −0.6 V. (4 V, 6 V) par output kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: Linear: V_out = a·V1 + b·V2. a = 1/2 = 0.5, b = −0.6/3 = −0.2. V_out = 0.5 × 4 + (−0.2) × 6 = 2 − 1.2 = 0.8 V. 0.4 V tab aata hai jab diye gaye outputs ko seedha jod dete ho (1 − 0.6) bina inputs ko scale kiye, aur 3.2 V me sign ulta ho gaya.

questions.question: 12 V source 4 Ω ke through node A se juda hai; A se ground tak 2 Ω hai; aur ek 3 A current source ground se A me current daalta hai. Source ka − terminal ground par hai. V_A kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Sirf 12 V (current source open): 12 × 2/6 = 4 V. Sirf 3 A (voltage source short): 4 Ω ∥ 2 Ω = 4/3 Ω, to 3 × 4/3 = 4 V. Total 8 V. 10 V tab aata hai jab current source ke case me shorted source wala 4 Ω path bhool kar sirf 2 Ω le lete ho (3 × 2 = 6).

questions.question: V1 = 10 V aur V2 = 5 V, dono 5 Ω ke through ek node se jude hain, aur node se ground tak 5 Ω load hai. Load me actual power kitni hai?
questions.explanation: Node voltage: (10/5 + 5/5)/(3/5) = 3/0.6 = 5 V. P = 5²/5 = 5 W. Agar har source ki akeli power jodo: V1 akela 10/3 V deta hai (2.22 W) aur V2 akela 5/3 V (0.56 W), sum 2.78 W — galat, kyunki power linear nahi hai.

weeks.title: Op-amp amplifiers, power signs and RC step response
weeks.summary: Is week aap ideal op-amp ke rules se inverting aur non-inverting amplifier design karoge, absorbed vs delivered power ka sign convention samjhoge, aur RC circuit ki charging/discharging (time constant τ = RC) seekhoge.
concepts: **Ideal op-amp**: gain bahut bada (infinite maano), input terminals me current zero, output resistance zero. Negative feedback ke saath do golden rules: (1) V+ = V− (virtual short), (2) inputs me current = 0. Output supply rails (jaise ±12 V) se bahar nahi ja sakta — wahan output **saturate** (clip) ho jaata hai.

**Non-inverting amplifier**: input V+ par, Rf output se V− tak, Rg V− se ground. V− = V_out·Rg/(Rf + Rg) = V_in ⇒ **gain = 1 + Rf/Rg**. Gain hamesha ≥ 1, sign same. Rf = 0 (ya Rg = ∞) par ye **buffer** (gain 1) ban jaata hai, jo source ko load nahi karta.

**Inverting amplifier**: V+ ground par, input Rin ke through V− par, Rf output se V− tak. V− = 0 (virtual ground), to Rin ka current Rf se hi jaata hai ⇒ **gain = −Rf/Rin**. Output ulta (180° phase shift) hota hai.

**Passive sign convention**: agar current element ke + terminal se andar jaata hai, to P = V × I absorbed power hai. P positive ⇒ element power le raha hai (resistor jaisa); P negative ⇒ power de raha hai (source jaisa). Poore circuit me saari absorbed powers ka sum = 0.

**RC charging**: 0 V wale capacitor ko R ke through Vs se jodo: v(t) = Vs(1 − e^(−t/τ)), **τ = RC**. t = τ par 63%, 5τ par ~99% charge. Current shuru me Vs/R hota hai aur exponentially zero ki taraf girta hai.
**RC discharging**: V0 par charged capacitor ko R se discharge karo: v(t) = V0·e^(−t/τ). V0 se V tak girne ka time t = τ·ln(V0/V). Har τ me voltage 37% reh jaata hai.

example.problem: Mic ka signal 0.3 V peak hai. Non-inverting amplifier me Rg = 2 kΩ aur Rf = 18 kΩ hai, supply ±12 V. Output peak kitna hoga? Agar input 1.5 V peak ho jaaye to kya hoga?
steps: 0.3 V input: output = 10 × 0.3 = 3 V peak (rails ke andar, theek).
1.5 V input: ideal output 15 V hona chahiye.
Par output +12 V se upar nahi ja sakta, isliye peaks 12 V par flat (clip) ho jaayenge — sound distort hogi.
Answer: **3 V peak; 1.5 V input par output ±12 V par clip**.

mistakes: Non-inverting gain ko Rf/Rg likh dena. Sahi formula 1 + Rf/Rg hai; −Rf/Rin sirf inverting ka hai.
Output ko rails se bada maan lena. Ideal formula ka answer supply se zyada aaye to output saturate hoga.
Discharge ka time nikaalte waqt ln(V0/V) ki jagah ln(V/V0) ya seedha ratio le lena.
revision: Ideal op-amp + negative feedback: V+ = V−, input current 0.
P = VI with current into +: positive = absorbed, negative = delivered.

questions.question: Inverting amplifier me Rin = 10 kΩ aur Rf = 47 kΩ hai. Input 0.2 V DC ho to output kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: Gain = −Rf/Rin = −47/10 = −4.7. V_out = −4.7 × 0.2 = −0.94 V. 1.14 V non-inverting formula (1 + 4.7) × 0.2 se aata hai, aur 0.94 V me minus sign chhoot gaya.

questions.question: R = 10 kΩ aur C = 100 μF wale RC circuit ka time constant kitna hai?
questions.explanation: τ = RC = 10 × 10³ × 100 × 10⁻⁶ = 1 s. kΩ (10³) aur μF (10⁻⁶) ke prefixes dhyaan se lagao; ek bhi galat hua to 1 ms ya 10 s jaise answer aate hain.

questions.question: Ek element ke across 5 V hai (+ terminal upar). 2 A current element ke − terminal se andar jaata hai aur + terminal se bahar nikalta hai. Element kitni power absorb karta hai?
questions.explanation: Passive convention me current + terminal se andar lena hota hai. Yahan current + se bahar nikal raha hai, to + se andar jaane wala current = −2 A. P_absorbed = 5 × (−2) = −10 W, yaani element 10 W deliver kar raha hai (source jaisa). +10 W direction check kiye bina V × I lene se aata hai.

questions.question: 0 V wala capacitor C = 50 μF, R = 2 kΩ ke through 10 V DC se t = 0 par joda gaya. t = 0.2 s par capacitor voltage kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: τ = 2000 × 50 × 10⁻⁶ = 0.1 s, to t = 0.2 s = 2τ. v = 10(1 − e⁻²) = 10(1 − 0.135) ≈ 8.65 V. 6.32 V sirf t = τ par hota hai, aur 1.35 V = 10e⁻² discharge wala formula hai.

questions.question: Non-inverting amplifier: Rf = 90 kΩ, Rg = 10 kΩ, supply ±12 V (output rails tak hi ja sakta hai). Input 1.5 V DC hai. Output kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: Gain = 1 + 90/10 = 10, to ideal output 15 V banta. Par output +12 V rail se upar nahi ja sakta, isliye 12 V par saturate. 15 V rails ignore karne se aata hai, aur 13.5 V gain ko Rf/Rg = 9 lene se.

questions.question: 100 μF capacitor 9 V par charged hai aur t = 0 par 10 kΩ resistor se discharge hona shuru hota hai. Voltage 3 V tak girne me kitna time lagega?
questions.explanation: τ = 10⁴ × 10⁻⁴ = 1 s. 3 = 9e^(−t/τ) ⇒ e^(−t) = 1/3 ⇒ t = ln 3 ≈ 1.10 s. 0.41 s tab aata hai jab ln(9/6) le lete ho (girawat 6 V ko target samajh kar), aur 0.33 s = 3/9 jo bina log ke ratio hai.

weeks.title: First-order RC filters: low-pass, high-pass, band-pass
weeks.summary: Is week aap RC low-pass aur high-pass filter ka frequency response, cutoff frequency fc = 1/(2πRC), dB scale, do filters ko cascade karke band-pass, aur first-order filters ki limitations (gentle slope, loading) seekhoge.
concepts: **Capacitor ka impedance**: Z_C = 1/(jωC), magnitude 1/(2πfC). Low frequency par bahut bada (DC par open), high frequency par chhota (short jaisa). Isi frequency-dependence se filter bante hain.

**RC low-pass**: R series me, output C ke across. |H| = 1/√(1 + (f/fc)²), jahan **fc = 1/(2πRC)**. f ≪ fc par |H| ≈ 1 (pass), f ≫ fc par |H| ≈ fc/f (har 10× frequency par 10× kam). Use: hiss/noise hatana, treble cut.
**RC high-pass**: C series me, output R ke across. |H| = (f/fc)/√(1 + (f/fc)²). DC par output 0, high f par ≈ 1. Use: DC block karna, 50 Hz hum ya rumble hatana.
**Cutoff frequency**: f = fc par dono filters ka |H| = 1/√2 ≈ 0.707, yaani power aadhi = −3 dB. Phase: low-pass −45°, high-pass +45°. dB me gain = 20·log10|H|; first-order slope = 20 dB/decade.
**Band-pass by cascading**: pehle high-pass (fc1) phir low-pass (fc2), fc1 < fc2. Beech ki frequencies pass hoti hain, jaise speech band 300 Hz–3.4 kHz. Ideal (buffered) gain = dono |H| ka product.

**Limitations**: (1) slope sirf 20 dB/decade, to fc se thoda bahar ki frequencies bhi kaafi pass hoti hain (2fc par bhi 0.447). (2) **Loading**: doosra stage pehle stage ko load karta hai, isliye bina buffer ke simple multiplication galat ho jaata hai. Fix: beech me op-amp buffer lagao ya doosre stage ka impedance ~10× bada rakho.

example.problem: Audio hiss kam karne ke liye low-pass filter: R = 10 kΩ, C = 10 nF. Cutoff frequency nikaalo, aur 100 Hz aur 5 kHz par gain batao.
steps: 100 Hz par f/fc ≈ 0.063: |H| = 1/√(1 + 0.004) ≈ 0.998 — lagbhag poora pass.
Matlab 5 kHz ka hiss sirf ~3× kam hua — first-order filter ka slope gentle hai.
Answer: **fc ≈ 1.6 kHz; gain ≈ 1.0 (100 Hz) aur ≈ 0.30 (5 kHz)**.

mistakes: fc = 1/(RC) likh dena. Hz me cutoff ke liye 2π zaroori hai: fc = 1/(2πRC); 1/(RC) to ω_c (rad/s) hai.
Low-pass aur high-pass me output kahan se lena hai, mix kar dena. Low-pass: output C ke across; high-pass: output R ke across.
Do RC stages ko bina buffer jod kar gains multiply kar dena. Loading se actual gain kam aata hai.
revision: Stages ke beech buffer lagao, warna loading.

questions.question: RC low-pass filter me R = 1 kΩ aur C = 0.1 μF hai. Cutoff frequency lagbhag kitni hai?
questions.explanation: RC = 10³ × 10⁻⁷ = 10⁻⁴ s. fc = 1/(2π × 10⁻⁴) ≈ 1592 Hz ≈ 1.59 kHz. 10 kHz tab aata hai jab 2π bhool kar 1/RC le lete ho — wo ω_c hai rad/s me, Hz nahi.

questions.question: RC low-pass filter me 2 V amplitude ka sinusoid exactly cutoff frequency par diya. Output amplitude kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: f = fc par |H| = 1/√2 ≈ 0.707. Output = 2 × 0.707 ≈ 1.41 V. 1 V tab aata hai jab −3 dB ko 'voltage aadha' samajh lete ho; asal me power aadhi hoti hai, voltage 0.707 guna.

questions.question: Ek first-order low-pass filter ka fc = 1 kHz hai. 1 V amplitude ka 10 kHz sinusoid input hai. Output amplitude lagbhag kitna hai?
questions.explanation: f/fc = 10: |H| = 1/√(1 + 100) = 1/√101 ≈ 0.0995 ≈ 0.1, yaani −20 dB. Output ≈ 0.1 V. 0.01 V tab aata hai jab slope 40 dB/decade (second-order) maan lete ho; first-order sirf 20 dB/decade girata hai.

questions.question: 50 Hz hum hatane ke liye RC high-pass filter ka fc = 100 Hz rakha. 50 Hz hum ka gain |H| kitna hai?
questions.explanation: f/fc = 0.5: |H| = 0.5/√(1 + 0.25) = 0.5/1.118 ≈ 0.447. 0.894 low-pass ka gain hai (1/√1.25) — filter type mix ho gaya. 0.5 tab aata hai jab √ wala hissa ignore kar dete ho. Hum sirf ~2× kam hua, jo first-order ki limitation dikhata hai.

questions.question: Speech band ke upar wale cutoff ke liye RC low-pass chahiye jiska fc = 3.4 kHz ho, aur R = 10 kΩ. C lagbhag kitna lo?
questions.explanation: C = 1/(2πR·fc) = 1/(2π × 10⁴ × 3400) ≈ 4.68 nF ≈ 4.7 nF. 29 nF 2π bhoolne se aata hai, aur 53 nF tab jab galti se lower cutoff 300 Hz ke liye calculate kar dete ho.

questions.question: Ek RC high-pass (C series, R shunt) ke output par seedha ek RC low-pass (R series, C shunt) joda, bina buffer. Dono stages me same R aur same C hai. f = 1/(2πRC) par poore cascade ka gain |H| kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Bina buffer ke doosra stage (R + Z_C) pehle stage ke shunt R ke parallel aa jaata hai. Poora circuit solve karo (ya ωRC = 1 rakh kar complex divider lagao) to |H| = 1/3 aata hai. 0.5 wo answer hai jo buffered stages me 0.707 × 0.707 multiply karke milta — loading ko ignore karne ka trap.

weeks.title: Superposition with mixed sources and power bookkeeping
weeks.summary: Is week aap voltage aur current dono sources wale circuits me superposition, homogeneity se scaling, aur har element ki absorbed power nikaal kar power balance (sum = 0) check karna practice karoge.
concepts: **Mixed sources**: superposition me ek time par ek hi source on rakho. Voltage source off = short (0 V), current source off = open (0 A). Dependent sources (agar hon) kabhi off nahi karte. Har case ka answer sign ke saath jodo.
**Homogeneity**: linear circuit me agar saare independent sources k guna kar do to har voltage aur current k guna ho jaata hai. Par power V²/R ya I²R hai, isliye power **k² guna** hoti hai.

**Linear response form**: kisi bhi output ko likh sakte ho: y = a·Vs + b·Is + .... Do measurements (ek-ek source on karke) se a aur b nikaal lo, phir kisi bhi naye source combination ka output turant mil jaata hai.

**Absorbed power**: passive convention se har element ke liye P = V × I (current + terminal me jaata hua). Resistor hamesha positive absorb karta hai. Source ka P negative ho to wo power de raha hai, positive ho to power le raha hai (jaise charging battery).
**Power balance**: KCL + KVL ka natija hai ki poore circuit ki absorbed powers ka sum exactly 0 hota hai. Ye apne answers check karne ka sabse accha tareeka hai.

**Source bhi power absorb kar sakta hai**: agar doosra source zyada strong ho, to current kisi voltage source ke + terminal me andar ghus sakta hai. Tab wo source power absorb karta hai — phone ki battery charging me bilkul yahi hota hai.

example.problem: 10 V source 2 Ω (R1) ke through node A se juda hai, A se ground tak 2 Ω (R2) hai, aur 2 A current source ground se A me current daalta hai. V_A nikaalo aur har element ki absorbed power se power balance check karo.
steps: Sirf 10 V (current source open): V_A = 10 × 2/4 = 5 V.
Sirf 2 A (voltage source short): R1 ∥ R2 = 1 Ω, to V_A = 2 × 1 = 2 V. Total V_A = 7 V.
R1 me current source se A ki taraf = (10 − 7)/2 = 1.5 A.
Absorbed powers: R1 = 1.5² × 2 = 4.5 W; R2 = 7²/2 = 24.5 W.
10 V source: 1.5 A uske + terminal se bahar nikal raha hai, to P = −10 × 1.5 = −15 W (deliver).
Current source: A (7 V) par 2 A push kar raha hai, P = −7 × 2 = −14 W (deliver).
Answer: **V_A = 7 V, power balance sahi hai**.

mistakes: Current source ko off karte waqt short kar dena. Current source off = open circuit.
Sources ko double karne par power bhi double maan lena. Power k² se scale hoti hai.
Har voltage source ko hamesha power dene wala maan lena. Current ki direction check karo; current + terminal me ghuse to source absorb kar raha hai.
revision: Superposition: V source → short, I source → open.
Sab sources × k ⇒ V, I × k, power × k².
y = a·Vs + b·Is: ek-ek source se a, b nikaalo.
Source ka absorbed P positive ⇒ wo charge ho raha hai.

questions.question: Superposition me jab kisi independent current source ko 'off' karte hain, to use kis se replace karte hain?
questions.explanation: Current source off = 0 A, aur jis branch me 0 A ho wo open circuit hai. Short circuit voltage source ke liye hota hai (0 V). Current source ko short karna sabse common galti hai.

questions.question: Ek linear resistive circuit ke saare independent sources double kar diye. Kisi ek resistor me dissipate hone wali power par kya asar hoga?
questions.explanation: Homogeneity se har current double hota hai. P = I²R, to power 2² = 4 guna. 'Double' tab lagta hai jab power ko bhi linear maan lete ho — power quadratic hai.

questions.question: 20 V source 4 Ω ke through node A se juda hai, A se ground tak 6 Ω hai, aur 5 A current source ground se A me current daalta hai. Source ka − terminal ground par hai. V_A kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Sirf 20 V: 20 × 6/10 = 12 V. Sirf 5 A (voltage source short): 4 ∥ 6 = 2.4 Ω, to 5 × 2.4 = 12 V. Total 24 V. 12 V sirf ek source ka contribution hai. Nodal se check: (24 − 20)/4 + 24/6 = 1 + 4 = 5 A ✓.

questions.question: 9 V source 3 Ω ke through node A se juda hai, A se ground tak 6 Ω hai, aur ek 1.5 A current source A se current nikaal kar ground me bhejta hai. 6 Ω resistor me neeche (A se ground) kitna current hai?
questions.explanation: Sirf 9 V: 9/(3 + 6) = 1 A neeche. Sirf current source (9 V short): 1.5 A A se nikal raha hai, jo 3 Ω aur 6 Ω me 6:3 ratio me baantta hai; 6 Ω ka hissa 1.5 × 3/9 = 0.5 A, upar ki taraf (−0.5 A). Total = 1 − 0.5 = 0.5 A (V_A = 3 V). 1.5 A tab aata hai jab current source ka contribution ka sign ulta le lete ho.

questions.question: Ek linear circuit me sirf Vs = 10 V (Is = 0) par output 4 V hai, aur sirf Is = 2 A (Vs = 0) par output 6 V. Vs = 5 V aur Is = −1 A dono saath hon to output kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: Output = a·Vs + b·Is. a = 4/10 = 0.4, b = 6/2 = 3 V/A. Output = 0.4 × 5 + 3 × (−1) = 2 − 3 = −1 V. 5 V tab aata hai jab current source ka sign ignore karke 2 + 3 jod dete ho.

questions.question: 20 V source 4 Ω ke through node A se juda hai, A se ground tak 6 Ω hai, aur 5 A current source ground se A me current daalta hai (V_A = 24 V aata hai). 20 V source kitni power absorb karta hai?
questions.explanation: 4 Ω me current source se A ki taraf = (20 − 24)/4 = −1 A, yaani 1 A A se source ke + terminal me ghus raha hai. P_absorbed = 20 × 1 = +20 W — source charge ho raha hai. Check: 4 Ω (4 W) + 6 Ω (96 W) + 20 V source (20 W) + current source (−24 × 5 = −120 W) = 0 ✓. −40 W tab aata hai jab sirf 20 V ke akele case ka current (2 A) le lete ho.

weeks.title: From analog to digital audio: sampling and ADCs
weeks.summary: Is week aap dekhoge ki analog audio digital kaise banta hai: time me sampling (aur aliasing), amplitude ko bits me quantize karna, sample-and-hold, flash ADC, aur capacitors ke beech charge sharing jo switched-capacitor circuits ki neev hai.
concepts: **Analog vs digital**: analog signal har time par koi bhi value le sakta hai. Digital me do kaam hote hain: time ko discrete karna (**sampling**) aur amplitude ko limited levels me round karna (**quantization**). Fayda: copy, store, transmit karne me noise jama nahi hota.

**Sampling aur Nyquist**: har Ts = 1/fs second par ek sample lo. Agar signal ki highest frequency fmax ho, to fs > 2·fmax chahiye. CD audio fs = 44.1 kHz, isliye ~22 kHz tak ka sound represent ho sakta hai, jo insaan ki sunne ki range (~20 kHz) se thoda upar hai.

**Aliasing**: agar fs/2 se upar ki frequency f sample ho jaaye to wo |f − k·fs| par ek nakli (alias) frequency jaisi dikhti hai. Jaise 7 kHz ko 10 kHz par sample karo to 3 kHz dikhega. Isliye ADC se pehle **anti-aliasing low-pass filter** lagate hain.

**Quantization**: N bits = 2ᴺ levels. Full-scale range FSR ho to step Δ = FSR/2ᴺ. Rounding se maximum error Δ/2. Har extra bit step ko aadha karta hai aur SNR ~6 dB badhata hai (16-bit audio ≈ 96 dB).

**Sample-and-hold**: ek switch aur capacitor. Switch band (sample) hone par capacitor input ko follow karta hai; switch khulne par (hold) capacitor wahi voltage pakde rakhta hai, taaki ADC ko conversion ke dauraan steady value mile.

**Flash ADC**: resistor ladder se 2ᴺ − 1 reference voltages banao aur har ek par ek comparator lagao. Input jitne references se bada hai, utne comparators 1 dete hain (thermometer code), jise encoder binary me badalta hai. Sabse fast, par comparators ki sankhya bits ke saath exponentially badhti hai.
**Charge sharing**: C1 (V1 par) aur C2 (V2 par) ko jodo to charge conserve hota hai: V = (C1V1 + C2V2)/(C1 + C2). Energy conserve nahi hoti — kuch energy switch/wire me heat ban jaati hai.

**Switched-capacitor resistor**: capacitor C ko frequency f par do nodes ke beech baar-baar switch karo. Har cycle me Q = C·ΔV charge jaata hai, to average current I = f·C·ΔV, yaani ye ek resistor R_eq = 1/(f·C) jaisa behave karta hai. Chip par bade resistors banane ka sasta tareeka.

example.problem: 3-bit flash ADC ka Vref = 8 V hai, aur ladder 8 barabar resistors ka hai. Input 5.3 V ho to kitne comparators 1 denge aur output code kya hoga?
steps: Comparators = 2³ − 1 = 7.
Ladder references: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 V (har step 8/8 = 1 V).
5.3 V input 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 V se bada hai, 6 aur 7 V se chhota.
To 5 comparators 1 denge: thermometer code (upar se neeche) 0011111.
Encoder 5 ko binary me badalta hai: 5 = 101.
Answer: **5 comparators high, output 101**.

mistakes: N-bit flash ADC me 2ᴺ comparators maan lena. 2ᴺ levels ke beech 2ᴺ − 1 boundaries hoti hain, to comparators 2ᴺ − 1.
Nyquist ka matlab fmax = fs samajhna. Maximum representable frequency fs/2 hai.
Charge sharing me energy conserve karna. Charge conserve hota hai, energy nahi.

questions.question: CD audio 44.1 kHz par sample hota hai. Theory ke hisaab se sabse badi kaunsi frequency bina aliasing ke represent ho sakti hai?
questions.explanation: Nyquist: maximum frequency = fs/2 = 44.1/2 = 22.05 kHz. 88.2 kHz tab aata hai jab rule ulta laga dete ho (2·fs), aur 44.1 kHz tab jab fmax = fs samajh lete ho.

questions.question: Ek 4-bit flash ADC me kitne comparators chahiye?
questions.explanation: 4 bits = 2⁴ = 16 levels. 16 levels ke beech 15 boundaries hoti hain, to 2⁴ − 1 = 15 comparators. 16 levels aur comparators ko mix karne ka trap hai, aur 4 bits ki sankhya hai.

questions.question: Ek 10-bit ADC ka input range 0 se 5 V hai. Uska quantization step (1 LSB) lagbhag kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Levels = 2¹⁰ = 1024. Δ = 5/1024 ≈ 4.88 mV. 5 mV tab aata hai jab 2¹⁰ ko 1000 maan lete ho, 9.77 mV jab 2⁹ = 512 se divide karte ho, aur 0.5 V jab bits (10) se hi divide kar dete ho.

questions.question: 7 kHz ka pure tone 10 kHz sampling rate par sample kiya, bina anti-aliasing filter ke. Samples ko wapas analog banane par kaunsi frequency sunai degi?
questions.explanation: fs/2 = 5 kHz, aur 7 kHz usse upar hai, to alias banega: |7 − 10| = 3 kHz. 7 kHz tab lagta hai jab Nyquist limit check nahi karte, aur 17 kHz (7 + 10) bhi ek image hai par reconstruction filter ke baad 0–5 kHz band me sirf 3 kHz bachta hai.

questions.question: 2 μF capacitor 6 V par charged hai. Use ek uncharged 1 μF capacitor ke saath parallel me jod diya. Final common voltage kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Charge conserve: Q = 2 μF × 6 V = 12 μC. Total C = 3 μF, to V = 12/3 = 4 V. 3 V tab aata hai jab capacitance dekhe bina voltage ka simple average (6 + 0)/2 le lete ho.

questions.question: 1 pF capacitor ko 100 kHz par baar-baar ek 1 V node aur ek 0 V node ke beech switch kiya jaata hai. Average current ke hisaab se ye kitne resistor jaisa behave karta hai?
questions.explanation: Har cycle me Q = CΔV = 10⁻¹² × 1 = 1 pC jaata hai. I = f·Q = 10⁵ × 10⁻¹² = 0.1 μA. R_eq = ΔV/I = 1/(f·C) = 1/(10⁵ × 10⁻¹²) = 10⁷ Ω = 10 MΩ. 1.59 MΩ capacitor ki reactance 1/(2πfC) hai — wo sinusoidal AC ke liye hoti hai, switching ke liye nahi.

weeks.title: Binary numbers, audio file sizes and digital building blocks
weeks.summary: Is week aap binary aur decimal ke beech conversion, audio data rate aur WAV file size ka hisaab, analog vs digital computing ka trade-off, aur logic gates se adder jaise basic digital blocks seekhoge.
concepts: **Binary number system**: base 2, digits sirf 0 aur 1. Har position ka weight 2 ki power: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, .... Jaise 1011 = 8 + 0 + 2 + 1 = 11. N bits se 0 se 2ᴺ − 1 tak ke numbers ban sakte hain (8 bits ⇒ 0–255).

**Decimal → binary**: baar-baar 2 se divide karo aur remainders likho; answer remainders ko **neeche se upar** padhne par milta hai. Ya phir sabse badi 2 ki power ghatao (38 = 32 + 4 + 2 ⇒ 100110). Hex (base 16) me 4 bits = 1 hex digit, jaise 1111 = F.

**Bits aur bytes**: 1 byte = 8 bits. Data rate aksar bits per second (bit/s) me, file size bytes me. Yahan 1 kB = 1000 bytes aur 1 MB = 10⁶ bytes le rahe hain (computers kabhi-kabhi 1024 bhi use karte hain).

**Audio data rate**: uncompressed (PCM/WAV) audio ka bit rate = sampling rate × bits per sample × channels. File size (bytes) = bit rate × duration ÷ 8, plus ek chhota header (WAV me ~44 bytes). MP3 jaise formats compression se size ~10× kam karte hain.

**Analog vs digital computing**: analog computer (op-amp adders, integrators) continuous voltages par seedha maths karta hai — fast aur kam power, par noise, drift aur component tolerance se accuracy limited. Digital computer numbers ko bits me rakhta hai — har stage par signal 0/1 me restore hota hai, isliye noise jama nahi hota aur precision bits badha kar badhayi ja sakti hai.

**Digital building blocks**: logic gates (NOT, AND, OR, XOR) se sab kuch banta hai. **Half adder**: Sum = A XOR B, Carry = A AND B. Full adder teen bits (A, B, carry-in) jodta hai; N full adders chain karke N-bit adder. Flip-flops/registers bits store karte hain, multiplexer kai inputs me se ek chunta hai.

example.problem: 3 minute ka stereo gaana 44.1 kHz par 16-bit samples me WAV file me save kiya. File size kitna hoga (header ignore karo, 1 MB = 10⁶ bytes)?
steps: Bytes per second = 1,411,200 ÷ 8 = 176,400 B/s.
Duration = 3 × 60 = 180 s.
Answer: **≈ 31.8 MB** (isi gaane ki 128 kbit/s MP3 sirf ~2.9 MB hoti).

mistakes: Division method me remainders ko upar se neeche padh lena. Pehla remainder sabse kam weight (LSB) ka hota hai, isliye neeche se upar padho.
bits ko bytes samajh lena. File size bytes me chahiye to 8 se divide karna mat bhoolo.
Stereo me channels = 2 bhool jaana. Mono ka size stereo ka aadha hota hai.
revision: Decimal → binary: ÷2 karo, remainders neeche se upar.
Bit rate = fs × bits × channels; bytes = bits ÷ 8.
Half adder: Sum = XOR, Carry = AND.
Digital: noise har stage par restore; analog: fast par noise jama hota hai.

questions.question: Decimal 38 ko binary me likho.
questions.explanation: 38 = 32 + 4 + 2 ⇒ 100110. Division se: remainders 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1 aate hain; neeche se upar padho to 100110. 011001 tab aata hai jab remainders upar se neeche padh lete ho — wo 25 hai.

questions.question: Binary 11010 ka decimal value kya hai?
questions.explanation: Weights 16, 8, 4, 2, 1: 16 + 8 + 0 + 2 + 0 = 26. 11 tab aata hai jab bits ko ulta (01011) padh lete ho, aur 13 ya 52 tab jab weights ek position khisak jaate hain.

questions.question: Landline jaisi digital voice: mono, 8 kHz sampling, 8 bits per sample. Bit rate kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Bit rate = 8000 × 8 × 1 = 64,000 bit/s = 64 kbit/s. 64 kbyte/s me bits aur bytes mix ho gaye (asli me 8 kbyte/s), aur 128 kbit/s stereo maan lene se aata hai.

questions.question: 1 minute ki stereo recording 48 kHz par 24-bit samples me hai. Uncompressed size kitna hai (1 MB = 10⁶ bytes, header ignore)?
questions.explanation: Bits = 48000 × 24 × 2 × 60 = 138,240,000. Bytes = ÷8 = 17,280,000 = 17.28 MB. 138.24 MB tab aata hai jab bits ko bytes me nahi badalte, 8.64 MB mono maan lene se, aur 0.288 MB sirf 1 second ka size hai.

questions.question: Half adder ke inputs A = 1 aur B = 1 hain. Outputs kya honge?
questions.explanation: Sum = A XOR B = 1 XOR 1 = 0, Carry = A AND B = 1. Binary me 1 + 1 = 10, yaani sum bit 0 aur carry 1. 'Sum = 1, Carry = 1' tab aata hai jab Sum ko OR samajh lete ho.

questions.question: Ek voice recorder me 10 MB (10 × 10⁶ bytes) memory hai. Wo mono audio 16 kHz par 12-bit samples me record karta hai (samples bina gap ke pack hote hain). Lagbhag kitne second ki recording aayegi?
questions.explanation: Memory = 10 × 10⁶ × 8 = 8 × 10⁷ bits. Bit rate = 16000 × 12 = 192,000 bit/s. Time = 8 × 10⁷ / 192,000 ≈ 417 s (≈ 7 min). 52 s tab aata hai jab bytes ko bits me badalna (×8) bhool jaate ho, 313 s jab har sample ko 16 bits me store maan lete ho, aur 208 s jab stereo maan lete ho.

weeks.title: Sending signals: cables, radio waves and modulation
weeks.summary: Is week aap wired links me delay, reflection aur ringing, radio waves ki wavelength aur antenna size, aur AM/FM modulation kyun aur kaise hota hai — ye sab simple numbers ke saath seekhoge.
concepts: **Wired link me delay**: cable me signal light ki speed se thoda dheere chalta hai, lagbhag v ≈ 2 × 10⁸ m/s (c ka ~2/3). 1 m cable ≈ 5 ns delay. Jab cable itni lambi ho ki ye delay signal ke rise time ke barabar ya zyada ho, to cable ko simple wire nahi maan sakte.

**Reflection aur termination**: har cable ka ek characteristic impedance Z0 hota hai (coax 50 Ω ya 75 Ω). Agar far end par load Z0 ke barabar na ho (jaise open end), to signal wapas reflect hota hai aur 2 × (length/v) baad sender par echo pahunchta hai. Matching resistor (= Z0) lagane se reflection khatam.

**Ringing**: reflections ya wires ka parasitic L aur C mil kar step ke baad oscillation (ringing) banate hain, jiski frequency ≈ 1/(2π√(LC)). Isse digital signals galat padhe ja sakte hain; termination aur chhote traces se ise kam karte hain.

**Radio waves**: EM waves free space me c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s par chalti hain. **Wavelength λ = c/f**. Achhi antenna ki length λ ke order ki hoti hai — common choice λ/4 (monopole) ya λ/2 (dipole). 100 MHz ⇒ λ = 3 m, quarter-wave 75 cm.

**Modulation kyun**: audio (20 Hz–20 kHz) ko seedha bhejne ke liye km-lambi antenna chahiye, aur sab stations ek hi band me takra jaayenge. Isliye audio ko ek high-frequency **carrier** par chadhaate hain: antenna chhoti, aur har station alag carrier frequency par.

**AM**: carrier ka amplitude audio ke hisaab se badalta hai. Single tone fm se carrier fc ke saath sidebands fc ± fm bante hain, bandwidth = 2fm. **Modulation index** m = (Vmax − Vmin)/(Vmax + Vmin) envelope se; m ≤ 1 rakho warna distortion.

**FM**: carrier ki frequency audio ke hisaab se badalti hai (peak deviation Δf). Bandwidth (Carson's rule) ≈ 2(Δf + fm). FM zyada bandwidth leta hai par amplitude noise se kam affect hota hai, isliye music ke liye better. India me AM medium wave ~0.5–1.7 MHz, FM 88–108 MHz.

example.problem: 5 kHz audio ko seedha radio wave bana kar bhejna ho to quarter-wave antenna kitni lambi chahiye? Usi audio ko 100 MHz FM carrier par bhejo to?
steps: Quarter-wave = 60/4 = 15 km — bilkul impractical.
100 MHz par λ = 3 × 10⁸ / 10⁸ = 3 m.
Quarter-wave = 3/4 = 0.75 m = 75 cm — car ya radio par aaraam se lag jaati hai.
Answer: **15 km vs 75 cm** — isi liye modulation zaroori hai.

mistakes: λ = c/f me MHz/GHz ko Hz me badalna bhool jaana. 2.4 GHz = 2.4 × 10⁹ Hz.
Cable reflection ka time nikaalte waqt sirf one-way delay le lena. Echo ko jaana aur wapas aana dono padta hai, yaani 2 × length/v.
AM ki bandwidth fm maan lena. Dono sidebands hote hain, isliye bandwidth 2fm hai.
revision: AM: sidebands fc ± fm, BW = 2fm, m = (Vmax − Vmin)/(Vmax + Vmin).

questions.question: 2.4 GHz WiFi signal ki free-space wavelength kitni hai?
questions.explanation: λ = c/f = 3 × 10⁸ / 2.4 × 10⁹ = 0.125 m = 12.5 cm. GHz ko 10⁹ ki jagah 10⁸ ya 10¹⁰ le lene par 1.25 m ya 1.25 cm aata hai — power of 10 dhyaan se.

questions.question: 1 MHz ke AM carrier ko ek single 5 kHz tone se modulate kiya. Output me kaunsi frequencies hongi?
questions.explanation: AM me carrier fc ke saath sidebands fc ± fm aate hain: 1000 ± 5 = 995 aur 1005 kHz. Bandwidth = 2 × 5 = 10 kHz. 990/1010 kHz tab aata hai jab sidebands ko fc ± 2fm samajh lete ho (bandwidth ko ek side ka offset maan kar).

questions.question: 900 MHz mobile band ke liye quarter-wave antenna ki length lagbhag kitni hogi?
questions.explanation: λ = 3 × 10⁸ / 9 × 10⁸ = 0.333 m = 33.3 cm. Quarter-wave = 33.3/4 ≈ 8.3 cm. 33.3 cm poori wavelength hai aur 16.7 cm half-wave — quarter lena bhool gaye.

questions.question: Oscilloscope par AM signal ka envelope maximum 12 V aur minimum 4 V (peak) tak jaata hai. Modulation index m kitna hai?
questions.explanation: m = (Vmax − Vmin)/(Vmax + Vmin) = (12 − 4)/(12 + 4) = 8/16 = 0.5. 0.33 = 4/12 seedha ratio hai, aur 0.67 = 8/12 me denominator galat hai.

questions.question: 20 m lambi cable ka far end open hai, aur cable me signal speed 2 × 10⁸ m/s hai. Sender par bheja gaya pulse reflect hokar kitne time baad wapas aayega?
questions.explanation: Pulse ko 20 m jaana aur 20 m wapas aana hai: 40 m / (2 × 10⁸ m/s) = 2 × 10⁻⁷ s = 200 ns. 100 ns sirf one-way delay hai, aur 133 ns tab aata hai jab cable me bhi light ki speed 3 × 10⁸ m/s le lete ho.

questions.question: Ek FM station 98.3 MHz par hai, peak deviation Δf = 75 kHz aur highest audio frequency fm = 15 kHz. Carson's rule se bandwidth aur quarter-wave antenna ki length kya hai?
questions.explanation: Bandwidth ≈ 2(Δf + fm) = 2(75 + 15) = 180 kHz. λ = 3 × 10⁸ / 98.3 × 10⁶ ≈ 3.05 m, quarter-wave ≈ 0.76 m = 76 cm. 30 kHz AM wala formula (2fm) hai, aur 3.05 m poori wavelength hai.

weeks.title: Capacitor energy puzzles and course recap
weeks.summary: Is aakhri week me aap capacitor energy, current source se capacitor charging, RC charging me hone wala energy loss, charge sharing aur stepwise charging jaise mixed problems solve karoge, aur poore course ka recap karoge.
concepts: **Capacitor energy**: E = ½CV² = Q²/(2C). Voltage double ⇒ energy 4 guna. Supercapacitor (jaise 10 F, 2.7 V) bhi sirf ~36 J store karta hai, jabki phone battery (~15 Wh) ~54,000 J — isliye supercaps fast burst ke liye, bulk storage ke liye nahi.

**Current source se charging**: constant I se capacitor charge karo to dV/dt = I/C, yaani voltage seedhi line (ramp) me badhta hai: V(t) = V0 + I·t/C. Ye ADC ke ramp generators aur timers me use hota hai.

**RC charging ka energy loss**: 0 V capacitor ko R ke through Vs se full charge karo. Source deta hai Q·Vs = CVs², capacitor store karta hai ½CVs², aur baaki **½CVs² resistor me heat** — R chahe kitna bhi ho! R sirf time (τ) badalta hai, loss nahi.

**Stepwise charging**: agar Vs ko N barabar steps me badhao (har step par capacitor ko settle hone do), to har step me loss ½C(Vs/N)², total = ½CVs²/N. Jitne zyada steps, utna kam loss — energy-efficient circuits (adiabatic charging) ka idea yahi hai.

**Charge sharing loss**: do capacitors jodne par charge conserve hota hai par energy ghatti hai. Do barabar capacitors (ek V par, ek 0 par) jodo to final V/2 aur aadhi energy heat ban jaati hai, connecting wire ka resistance chahe kitna bhi chhota ho.

**Course recap**: gadget ko blocks me dekho (week 1) → circuit laws aur analysis (weeks 2, 4, 5, 8) → time-varying signals aur RC (weeks 3, 6, 7) → digital duniya (weeks 9, 10) → communication (week 11). Har problem me units, sign convention aur sanity check se answer verify karo.

example.problem: 2 mA constant current source ek 100 μF capacitor (shuru me 0 V) ko charge karta hai. 5 V tak pahunchne me kitna time lagega, aur tab capacitor me kitni energy hogi?
steps: Time to 5 V = 5/20 = 0.25 s.
Charge check: Q = I·t = 2 × 10⁻³ × 0.25 = 0.5 mC = C·V = 100 μF × 5 V ✓.
Energy = ½CV² = ½ × 100 × 10⁻⁶ × 25 = 1.25 mJ.

mistakes: Socha ki chhota R lagane se charging ka energy loss kam hoga. Ek step me charging ka loss hamesha ½CVs² hai, R se independent.
Charge sharing me energy conservation laga dena. Charge conserve karo (Q = CV), phir energy alag se nikaalo.
½CV² me ½ bhool jaana, ya μF/mJ ke prefixes mix karna.
revision: RC charging: source CV², capacitor ½CV², resistor ½CV².
N steps me charging: loss = ½CV²/N.
Equal caps sharing (V aur 0): final V/2, aadhi energy loss.

questions.question: 1 F ka supercapacitor 5 V tak charged hai. Usme kitni energy store hai?
questions.explanation: E = ½CV² = ½ × 1 × 25 = 12.5 J. 25 J ½ bhoolne se aata hai, aur 5 J = C × V (wo charge Q = 5 C hai, energy nahi).

questions.question: 1 mA ka constant current source 10 μF capacitor (shuru me 0 V) ko 20 ms tak charge karta hai. Capacitor ka voltage kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: V = I·t/C = 10⁻³ × 20 × 10⁻³ / 10 × 10⁻⁶ = 2 × 10⁻⁵ / 10⁻⁵ = 2 V. 0.2 V ya 20 V ms aur μF ke prefixes me ek galti se aate hain.

questions.question: 0 V wala 100 μF capacitor 1 kΩ resistor ke through 10 V DC source se poora charge kiya gaya. Is process me resistor me kitni energy heat bani?
questions.explanation: Source ne diya Q·V = CV² = 100 × 10⁻⁶ × 100 = 10 mJ. Capacitor me store hua ½CV² = 5 mJ. Baaki 10 − 5 = 5 mJ resistor me heat. 10 mJ source ki total energy hai, aur 0 mJ tab lagta hai jab sochte ho ki saari energy capacitor me chali gayi.

questions.question: 10 μF capacitor 8 V par charged hai. Use ek uncharged 10 μF capacitor se jod diya. Is process me kitni energy lose (heat) hui?
questions.explanation: Pehle: ½ × 10 μF × 64 = 320 μJ. Charge 80 μC, total C = 20 μF, final V = 4 V. Baad me: ½ × 20 μF × 16 = 160 μJ. Loss = 320 − 160 = 160 μJ. 0 μJ energy conserve maan lene ka trap hai, aur 320 μJ shuru ki poori energy.

questions.question: Back-of-the-envelope: ek phone battery 15 Wh store karti hai. Utni energy store karne ke liye 10 F, 2.7 V ke kitne supercapacitors (full charged) chahiye honge?
questions.explanation: 15 Wh = 15 × 3600 = 54,000 J. Ek supercap: ½ × 10 × 2.7² ≈ 36.5 J. N ≈ 54,000/36.5 ≈ 1480 ≈ 1500. 150 tab aata hai jab Wh ko J me badalte waqt 3600 ki jagah 360 le lete ho. Isse samajh aata hai ki supercaps bulk energy ke liye kyun nahi hain.

questions.question: 100 μF capacitor (0 V) ko resistor ke through 10 V tak charge karna hai, par do steps me: pehle source 5 V (poora settle hone do), phir source 10 V. Dono steps me resistor me total kitni energy heat bani?
questions.explanation: Har step me voltage jump 5 V hai, aur ek step ka loss = ½C(ΔV)² = ½ × 100 × 10⁻⁶ × 25 = 1.25 mJ. Do steps: 2 × 1.25 = 2.5 mJ. Ek hi step (0 → 10 V) me loss 5 mJ hota — steps se loss aadha ho gaya. 1.25 mJ sirf ek step ka loss hai.
